extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma what a person should do, knowing that time destroys all beings and life is short.
Bhishma recounts an ancient dialogue between a father and son to answer Yudhishthira's question.

attributes.context: Bhishma begins teaching through a parable.

extraction_text: A Brahmin father, devoted to Vedic study, has a wise son named Medhavin (Wise).
Medhavin, knowledgeable about liberation and truth, asks his father what a wise person should do, seeing human life is brief.

attributes.action: Son seeks guidance on righteous action.

extraction_text: The father advises studying Vedas, observing celibacy, having sons to purify ancestors, maintaining sacred fires, performing rituals, and finally retiring to the forest to become a sage.

attributes.action: Prescribes orthodox duties and stages of life.

extraction_text: Medhavin challenges his father, asking how he can speak so calmly when the world is attacked, besieged, and struck fatally without fail.
The father asks for clarification on what attacks the world, who besieges it, and what the unfailing strikes are.
Medhavin explains that the world is attacked by death, besieged by old age, and struck fatally day and night by time.

attributes.action: Identifies death, old age, and time as relentless forces.

extraction_text: Medhavin urges immediate action, stating that death does not wait for tasks to be completed and can come unexpectedly, like a wolf snatching a lamb.

attributes.action: Advocates for diligence and urgency in righteous deeds.

extraction_text: Medhavin advises practicing righteousness in youth, as life is fleeting, to gain fame and happiness in this life and the next.

attributes.action: Emphasizes early adherence to dharma for dual rewards.

extraction_text: Medhavin warns that death takes those obsessed with sons, cattle, wealth, or unfinished tasks, just as a flood carries away a sleeping tiger.

attributes.action: Criticizes attachment to worldly affairs as perilous.

extraction_text: Medhavin concludes by questioning how one can live in apparent ease when death, old age, and disease afflict the body from birth until death, controlling all beings.

attributes.action: Highlights the inevitability of suffering and mortality.

extraction_text: The text discusses philosophical teachings about life, death, truth, and liberation.

key_points: Villages are described as the abode of death and bondage
Forests are described as the cow-pen of the gods
Truth is presented as the only defense against death
Non-violence in thought, word, and deed leads to liberation
Knowledge, truth, and self-control are praised as supreme virtues

extraction_text: The narrator declares personal spiritual practices and rejection of violent sacrifices.

key_points: Rejection of animal sacrifices and destructive Kshatriya rituals
Commitment to peaceful sacrifices, truth, and self-control
Declaration of independence from descendants for salvation
Emphasis on finding the Self hidden in the cave

extraction_text: Bhishma concludes the teaching by urging action based on the son's words.

key_points: Bhishma recounts that the father followed the son's advice
Urges the listener (King) to act accordingly
Emphasizes dedication to truth and dharma
